question.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned} & x+2z=3 \\  & -2x+y-3z=-4 \\  & 4x-3y+6z=-8\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & 3 \\ -2 & 1 & -3 & -4 \\ 4 & -3 & 6 & -8\end{aligned}].
$$

Transforming $M$ to reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & 3 \\ -2 & 1 & -3 & -4 \\ 4 & -3 & 6 & -8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 4 & -3 & 6 & -8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-4){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & -3 & -2 & -20\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+3{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -14\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 16 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -14\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-2){R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 31 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 16 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -14\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\{\begin{aligned} & x=31 \\  & y=16 \\  & z=-14.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the solution $x=31$, $y=16$ and $z=-14.$ Or, in vector form $⟨31,16,-14⟩.$
